capabilities.target: any customer account record, by email or account id

instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer by email or account id, not only the person who sent the ticket.
Human review is skipped by default and only triggered when the model itself judges the customer to be angry.
The sole control against leaking another customer's data to the requester is a prompt instruction, which is behavioral and depends on model compliance.
The agent is positioned as sole decision maker for classification, lookup, drafting, and sending, with no default human checkpoint.

controls.name: Prompt instruction against cross-customer sharing
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to follow a prompt rule. A more capable or injected model can rationalize exceptions (for example, deciding the requester 'is' the other customer) or split the disclosure into steps that each look compliant.

controls.name: Escalate to a human only when the customer appears angry
controls.decay_rationale: The decision to escalate is made by the model from inferred sentiment, not a structural check. It can be bypassed by phrasing or injected content, and decays further as the model gets better at rationalizing routine handling.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the ticket record
controls.decay_rationale: Binding the send destination to the address on the originating ticket record, read from the system of record rather than chosen by the model, makes an attacker-controlled or cross-customer destination unreachable regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Least-privilege CRM credential scoped to the requester's own record
controls.decay_rationale: A credential that can only resolve the record matching the authenticated sender removes the ability to read other customers' data regardless of what the model is told to do.

controls.name: Human approval gate on outbound email, raw action review
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate does not decay with model capability. It remains independent as long as approval volume stays low enough to avoid approval fatigue.

controls.name: Mail credential scoped away from a single shared send-to-any-address token
controls.decay_rationale: Replacing the shared service account token with per-ticket or domain-restricted send scope narrows the blast radius independent of model behavior.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta and confused deputy (TC1 + TC4): untrusted email drives unrestricted CRM read and unrestricted send

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email enters triage as a new ticket
Agent may look up any customer by email or account id, not just the requester, using a broad-scope service token
Agent sends the drafted reply, which may include CRM data, to any address using a shared service account token with no destination confirmation

forecast.watch_signal: The model/version string in runtime config changes with no separate review (subject.model.swappable is true), or prompt.md lines 5-6 and 14 are edited, weakened, or removed.

evidence.observation: Agent is told it 'may look up any customer by email or account id,' not limited to the person emailing.
Routine tickets are sent directly with no human review; escalation only occurs if the model judges the customer 'angry.'
The only safeguard against leaking another customer's data is a prompt instruction ('Never share another customer's information...').
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are reached with static bearer tokens (CRM_SVC_TOKEN, MAIL_SVC_TOKEN), with no per-user scoping declared.

CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address; outbound email is only logged to the SIEM, not gated; the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review.

recommendations.action: Scope the CRM credential so it can only resolve the record matching the authenticated requester, not an arbitrary email or account id supplied in the ticket.
Bind the outbound send address to the address on the originating ticket record rather than a model-chosen or confirmed address, and stop relying on a single shared send-to-any-address token.
Add a raw-action human approval gate before any outbound email that includes CRM data for an account identifier that does not match the sender's verified email.
Replace the sentiment-based escalation rule with a structural rule requiring approval whenever the resolved account does not match the sender's verified email.

rating.rationale: One finding drives the rating: an untrusted customer email can direct an unrestricted CRM lookup (broad-scope token, any email or account id) and an unrestricted send (shared service account token, any address), reaching an S3 sink (irreversible egress of confidential data) with no default human review (A4 fully autonomous). Inherent is critical (U source x S3 sink). The only present controls are two behavioral, model-dependent prompt rules (no cross-customer sharing; escalate only if angry) plus detective SIEM logging, which earns no tier credit. Per rubric section 5 step 4, the two dependent controls together give a single -1 tier credit, so residual is high; no structural control (scoped credential, destination confirmation, or raw-action approval gate) is present to narrow or sever the path. Under a model upgrade, or removal of the prompt rules, both behavioral controls are expected to fail first and the finding reverts to critical, which sets the forecast. The control whose decay moves the forecast most is control.prompt_no_share.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest or MCP server-side schema was provided beyond the two tool references named in prompt.md; argument-level validation, rate limiting, and sandboxing could not be assessed and are assumed absent.

Autonomy level (A4_fully_autonomous) is inferred from the absence of any declared review step beyond conditional, sentiment-based escalation; it is not explicitly stated in the artifacts, so confidence on that classification is medium.
